category: PSpice Probe trace expressions: output variables, operators, analog functions, digital constants and macros
description: The expression language accepted by Trace > Add Trace (and by measurement arguments, macros and Performance Analysis) in the PSpice waveform viewer: analog output variables and their AC suffix forms, device noise variables, sweep variables, arithmetic and section-selection operators, the full list of analog functions from the PSpice 17.4 help (ABS through TAN), digital signal and bus constants and operators, and user macros stored in .prb files.

tools.name: V() (Probe voltage trace)
tools.description: Plots a node voltage referenced to ground, or the difference between two nodes, from the waveform data file. In Probe the node can be a net name, a hierarchical path or a device pin written as <refdes>:<pin>, which is how Capture markers name pin voltages. It is the most common trace and the usual argument of every other function and measurement.

parameters.name: <node>
parameters.description: Net alias, auto-generated net name (N12345), or pin reference such as R1:2.

tools.example: Trace > Add Trace: V(out)   V(in,out)   V(Q1:c)   V(X_U1.N004)
tools.notes: Per the PSpice help, the two-terminal-device form V(R3) and the Vxy(device) form such as VCE(Q13) that .PRINT accepts are not valid Probe trace names; use pin voltages or node names instead. The list only offers what the data collection settings saved (see Data Collection tab).

tools.name: I() (Probe current trace)
tools.description: Plots the current through a device or into a device pin. The positive direction is into the first (positive) node of the device, so I(R1) is positive when current flows from pin 1 to pin 2, and I(V1) of a supply is negative while the supply delivers power. Capture's Current Into Pin marker produces the pin form I(<refdes>:<pin>).

parameters.name: <device>
parameters.description: Reference designator as netlisted, e.g. R1, V1, L3, or R_R1 in hierarchical/netlisted form.

parameters.name: Ix
parameters.description: Terminal letter for 3/4-terminal devices, e.g. IC(Q1), IB(Q1), ID(M1), IG(M1).

tools.example: Trace > Add Trace: I(R1)   -I(V1)   IC(Q1)/IB(Q1)   I(L1:1)
tools.notes: Plot -I(Vsupply) to see a positive supply current. Currents of controlled sources (E, F, G, H) are not always saved; insert a 0 V source in series when you need a guaranteed current probe.

tools.name: W() (Probe power trace)
tools.description: Plots instantaneous power dissipated by a device (voltage across times current through it), the quantity written by Capture's Power Dissipation marker. Wrap it in AVG() or RMS() to turn the instantaneous waveform into a running average for thermal and efficiency work.

parameters.name: <device>
parameters.description: Any device for which power data was collected (the Power option on the Data Collection tab).

tools.notes: Sources that deliver energy show negative W(). Power data is only available when power collection was enabled in the simulation profile.

tools.name: Vx() / Ix() (terminal-specific traces)
tools.description: Terminal-specific voltage and current forms for semiconductors and other multi-terminal devices, where x is the terminal letter. They let you plot the gate voltage of a MOSFET or the base current of a BJT without knowing the node names connected to the pins.
tools.usage: Vx(<device>) / Ix(<device>) with x = terminal letter (Q: C B E S, M: D G S B, J: D G S, B: D G S, Z: C G E)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Terminal letter of the device type.

tools.notes: Two-letter voltage forms (VCE, VGS) are .PRINT syntax; in Probe write VC(Q1)-VE(Q1) or use pin voltages.

tools.name: VDB() / VP() / VG() / VR() / VI() / VM() (AC trace suffixes)
tools.description: Shorthand suffixes for AC-analysis traces: M magnitude, DB decibels, P phase in degrees, G group delay in seconds, R real part and I imaginary part, applicable to V and I variables. They are equivalent to wrapping the variable in M(), DB(), P(), G(), R() or IMG() and are what the Capture 'Advanced' markers generate.
tools.usage: V<suffix>(<node>)  |  I<suffix>(<device>) with suffix M, DB, P, G, R, I
tools.example: Bode plot: VDB(out) on the first Y axis, VP(out) on a second Y axis (Plot > Add Y Axis).
tools.notes: Only meaningful for AC sweep data. For transient data use DB() only on already-positive quantities.

tools.name: Device noise traces (NTOT, NFID, NSID, NRB, NRC, NRD, NRE, NRG, NRS, NFIB, NSIB, NSIC, NRHI, NRLO)
tools.description: Per-device noise contributions available in Probe after a noise analysis, written N<noise_type>(<device>). They show which transistor or resistor dominates the output noise, complementing the totals V(ONOISE), V(INOISE) and I(INOISE). NTOT is the total contribution of the device.

parameters.name: Q (BJT)
parameters.description: NFIB base flicker, NRB/NRC/NRE thermal, NSIB base shot, NSIC collector shot, NTOT.

parameters.name: M (MOSFET)
parameters.description: NFID drain flicker, NRB/NRD/NRG/NRS thermal, NSID drain shot, NTOT.

parameters.name: D, J, B
parameters.description: NFID, NRS (+NRD, NRG for J/B), NSID, NTOT.

parameters.name: R, S, W, O
parameters.description: NTOT only; N (digital input) adds NRHI and NRLO.

tools.example: .NOISE V(out) Vin 10 in the profile, then Trace > Add Trace: V(ONOISE)  NTOT(R1)  NTOT(Q1)
tools.notes: Generated only when a noise analysis runs. Device contributions are power densities (V^2/Hz) while V(ONOISE) is V/sqrt(Hz); take SQRT() before comparing.

tools.name: Time / Frequency / swept-source names (X-axis and sweep variables)
tools.description: The independent variable of each analysis is itself a trace variable: Time for transient data, Frequency for AC data, and the name of the swept source (or parameter) for DC sweeps. It can be used inside expressions, for example to build a window function or a reference ramp, and selected as the X axis variable in Plot > Axis Settings.
tools.usage: Time  |  Frequency  |  V1 (name of the swept DC source)
tools.example:
Plot V(out) versus V(in) for a transfer curve: Plot > Axis Settings > X Axis > Axis Variable = V(in).
Hann-weighted signal before FFT: V(out)*0.5*(1-COS(2*3.14159*Time/10m))
tools.notes: Documented Probe Fourier mode has no selectable window function; multiplying by an explicit window expression of Time, over an integral number of periods, is the usual workaround for leakage.

tools.name: ( ) * / + - (analog trace operators)
tools.description: Arithmetic operators for combining output variables, constants and functions in a trace expression, evaluated with normal precedence and parentheses for grouping. For AC data Probe performs complex arithmetic and displays the magnitude of a complex result, so V(4)+V(5) is always positive while IMG(V(4)+V(5)) can be negative.
tools.notes: Numeric suffixes (m, u, n, k, meg) are accepted in constants. There is no ** power operator in Probe; use PWR(x,y).

tools.name: @ (section and data-file selector)
tools.description: Restricts a trace to one data section (one run of a parametric, temperature or Monte Carlo sweep) and/or one of several loaded data files. It is how you compare a single Monte Carlo run with the nominal run or overlay results from two different simulations.
tools.notes: Right-click a trace > Information shows which section and file it came from.

tools.name: #n (reference to an existing trace)
tools.description: Refers to a trace that is already displayed in the Probe window by its position number, so a derived trace can be built without retyping long expressions. If V(in) is trace 1 and V(out) is trace 2, #2/#1 plots the gain.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Order in which the trace was added to the window.

tools.notes: Numbers follow the add order; deleting traces renumbers them, so prefer explicit expressions in saved displays or macros.

tools.name: ; (trace display name)
tools.description: A semicolon after a trace expression gives the trace a legend name different from the expression text; for digital buses a second semicolon field sets the radix. It keeps plots readable when expressions are long.

parameters.name: <radix>
parameters.description: Bus radix H/X, D, O or B.

tools.name: ABS(x)
tools.description: Absolute value |x| of a trace, point by point. Used to rectify signals before averaging, or to plot current magnitude regardless of direction.

tools.name: SGN(x)
tools.description: Sign function returning +1 when x > 0, 0 when x = 0 and -1 when x < 0. Useful for building comparator-style or polarity-dependent derived traces and in marked point expressions.

tools.name: SQRT(x)
tools.description: Square root of a trace. Typical uses are converting noise power densities to V/sqrt(Hz) and computing RMS from an integral.
tools.example: SQRT(S(V(ONOISE)*V(ONOISE)))   (integrated output noise over the swept band)

tools.name: EXP(x)
tools.description: Natural exponential e^x of a trace, point by point. Used for reconstructing diode or thermal-model expressions in post-processing.

tools.name: LOG(x)
tools.description: Natural logarithm ln(x) of a trace. Note that LOG is base e in Probe; use LOG10 for base 10.
tools.notes: A frequent mistake is to use LOG() expecting decibels; use DB() or 20*LOG10(M(x)).

tools.name: LOG10(x)
tools.description: Base-10 logarithm of a trace. Combined with M() it reproduces DB() explicitly, or it can scale a quantity for a decade-style readout.

tools.name: PWR(x,y)
tools.description: Raises x to the power y. It is the only exponentiation available in Probe trace expressions, which have no ** operator.

tools.name: SIN(x) / COS(x) / TAN(x)
tools.description: Trigonometric functions of a trace with the argument in radians. Used to build reference waveforms, window functions or phase-dependent quantities such as real power from magnitude and phase.
tools.notes: P() returns degrees, so convert to radians before COS().

tools.name: ATAN(x) / ARCTAN(x)
tools.description: Arc tangent of a trace with the result in radians; ATAN and ARCTAN are synonyms. Used to compute phase from real and imaginary parts or from quadrature signals.
tools.notes: Single-argument only, so the result is limited to +/-90 degrees; P() handles all quadrants.

tools.name: D(x) (derivative)
tools.description: Derivative of x with respect to the X-axis variable (Time, Frequency or the swept source). dV(node) is shorthand for D(V(node)). It gives slew rate, small-signal conductance from a DC sweep, or inductor voltage from current.
tools.example:
D(V(out))/1e6   (slew rate in V/us)
DC sweep of V1: D(I(D1)) = small-signal diode conductance
tools.notes: Lower-case d() and upper-case D() are the same function. Do not confuse with the digital D(node) trace form. Derivatives of coarse data are noisy; tighten the maximum step size.

tools.name: S(x) (integral)
tools.description: Running integral of x over the range of the X-axis variable; sIC(node) style shorthand applies as with d(). Integrating power gives energy, integrating current gives charge, and integrating a noise density over frequency gives total noise.
tools.example:
S(W(M1))   (switching energy in joules)
S(I(C1))  (charge into C1)
tools.notes: The integral starts at the first displayed X value; restrict the X range with Plot > Axis Settings > Use Data > Restricted to integrate over one period.

tools.name: AVG(x)
tools.description: Running average of x from the start of the X-axis range up to each point, i.e. S(x)/elapsed X. The final value of the trace is the average over the whole displayed range, which is how average power or DC output level is read.
tools.example: AVG(W(Rload))   then read the last point with a cursor or YatLastX(AVG(W(Rload)))
tools.notes: Because it averages from the start, start-up transients bias the result; use AVGX() or restrict the X range to steady state.

tools.name: AVGX(x,d)
tools.description: Moving average of x over a sliding window of width d on the X axis, from X-d to X at each point. Setting d to one switching period gives the cycle-averaged waveform of a converter, which reveals the low-frequency envelope and settling behaviour.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Averaging window in X-axis units (seconds for transient).

tools.example: AVGX(V(sw),10u)   (100 kHz switching node averaged per cycle)

tools.name: RMS(x)
tools.description: Running RMS of x over the X-axis range, sqrt(S(x^2)/elapsed X). The final value is the RMS over the displayed range, used for ripple current in capacitors and RMS current in MOSFETs and windings.
tools.example: RMS(I(C_out))   read at the last point, or YatLastX(RMS(I(C_out)))
tools.notes: Like AVG it accumulates from the first point; restrict the range to an integer number of periods in steady state for a meaningful value.

tools.name: MAX(x)
tools.description: Maximum value of x, displayed as a constant trace across the plot. Handy for overlaying a peak level and for quick expressions like percentage ripple.
tools.notes: For a numeric result per run (Performance Analysis, Advanced Analysis) use the Max measurement rather than the MAX() trace function.

tools.name: MIN(x)
tools.description: Minimum value of x, displayed as a constant trace. The counterpart of MAX() for trough levels and peak-to-peak expressions.

tools.name: ENVMAX(x,d)
tools.description: Upper envelope of x built from its peaks; a point counts as a peak only if it is higher than d consecutive neighbouring data points. It extracts the envelope of modulated or ringing waveforms without an explicit detector circuit.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Minimum number of consecutive data points on each side defining a peak.

tools.notes: Result depends on the density of simulation points; limit the maximum time step so every carrier cycle has several points.

tools.name: ENVMIN(x,d)
tools.description: Lower envelope of x built from its valleys, where a valley must be lower than d consecutive neighbouring points. Used with ENVMAX() to plot modulation depth or peak-to-peak ringing envelopes.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Minimum consecutive points defining a valley.

tools.name: DB(x)
tools.description: Magnitude of x in decibels, 20*log10(|x|). It is the standard Bode magnitude function for AC data and also converts FFT magnitudes to dB in Fourier mode.
tools.notes: Equivalent to the VDB()/IDB() suffix form for a single variable, but also works on ratios and expressions.

tools.name: M(x)
tools.description: Magnitude of a complex AC quantity (linear). It is what Probe displays by default for complex results, but writing it explicitly documents intent and is required inside other functions.

tools.name: P(x)
tools.description: Phase of a complex AC quantity in degrees. Used for Bode phase plots, loop-gain phase margin and impedance angle.
tools.notes: Phase may be unwrapped beyond +/-180 degrees; account for that in measurement levels.

tools.name: R(x)
tools.description: Real part of a complex AC quantity. Real-valued results can be negative, unlike magnitudes, so it is the right function for equivalent series resistance or real input impedance.

tools.name: IMG(x)
tools.description: Imaginary part of a complex AC quantity. Used for reactance plots and to find resonance where the imaginary part crosses zero.
tools.example: IMG(V(a)/I(L1))   then ZeroCross() to find resonance

tools.name: G(x) (group delay)
tools.description: Group delay of a complex AC quantity in seconds, the negative derivative of phase with respect to angular frequency. It evaluates delay flatness of filters and equalisers; VG() and IG() are the suffix shorthands.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Complex trace expression (normally a transfer ratio).

tools.notes: Needs a dense AC sweep (many points per decade) for a smooth result.

tools.name: Trace > Macros (Probe macro definitions)
tools.description: Defines named, parameterised trace-expression macros that can be used anywhere a trace expression is accepted, and stores them in the [Macros] section of a .prb file. Macros can call other macros but not recursively, and are loaded, saved to other .prb files or deleted from the same dialog.

parameters.name: Save / Save To
parameters.description: Store in the current or another .prb file.

parameters.name: Load / Delete / Delete From
parameters.description: Manage macros from global or remote .prb files.

tools.example:
PI = 3.14159
GAIN(A,B) = DB(A/B)
PAVG(D) = AVG(W(D))  ; average power of a device
then Trace > Add Trace: GAIN(V(out),V(in))
tools.notes: Maximum 80 characters including name and arguments, no spaces inside the argument list; deleting a macro used by a displayed trace deletes that trace.

tools.name: Digital signal constants ('0 '1 'F 'R 'X 'Z)
tools.description: Constant logic states that can be used in digital trace expressions: '0 low, '1 high, 'F falling, 'R rising, 'X unknown, 'Z high impedance. They are compared or combined with digital signals to build qualifying expressions such as enable-gated clocks.

tools.name: Digital bus constants (r'ddd)
tools.description: Constant values for bus arithmetic and comparison in digital trace expressions, written as a lower-case radix letter, an apostrophe and digits. They let you add offsets to address buses or compare a data bus with an expected value.

parameters.name: radix
parameters.description: h or x hexadecimal, d decimal, o octal, b binary (must be lower case).

tools.name: Digital trace operators (~ * / + - & ^ |)
tools.description: Operators for digital trace expressions in precedence order: ( ) grouping, ~ complement, * / multiply and divide (bus values only), + - add and subtract (bus values only), & AND, ^ XOR, | OR. Operations between buses produce a bus wide enough for the result; bus-with-signal operations produce a bus.
tools.example:
~RESET & CLK
{D3 D2 D1 D0} ^ {Q3 Q2 Q1 Q0};MISMATCH;B
tools.notes: Select 'Digital Operators and Functions' in the Add Traces dialog to insert them; bus signals are listed high-order first and up to 32 bits.

tools.name: {bus_prefix[msb:lsb]} (bus range shorthand)
tools.description: Compact way to add a bus trace of up to 32 signals whose names share a prefix and differ only by index, instead of listing every bit. Display name and radix follow as optional semicolon fields.
tools.example: {a[3:0]};ADDR;D   is the same as {a3 a2 a1 a0};ADDR;D
